text: Top Vietnamese leader meets Russian President at APEC Economic Leaders' Week 2026

General Secretary and President To Lam of Vietnam on November 18 afternoon met President of Russia Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, China, on the sidelines of the APEC Economic Leaders' Week 2026, according the Vietnam News Agency.

General Secretary and President Lam told President Putin that Vietnam highly appreciates the role and contributions of the Russian Federation within APEC and requested Russia's support for the successful organization of APEC Year 2027 to be hosted by Vietnam.
The top Vietnamese leader also extended a cordial invitation to President Putin to attend the APEC Economic Leaders' Week 2027 in Phu Quoc, in conjunction with an official bilateral visit to Vietnam.
During the meeting, the two leaders highly valued the achievements made in continuously advancing the Vietnam-Russia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.

General Secretary and President Lam stated that immediately following his state visit to the Russian Federation in September 2026, Vietnam formulated an action plan with specific objectives and timelines, focusing on the implementation of strategic projects and cooperation in key sectors.
The two leaders agreed to continue strengthening delegation exchanges and high-level contacts through Party, State, Government, and National Assembly channels.

They also agreed to enhance the effectiveness of bilateral cooperation mechanisms, including the Vietnam-Russia Intergovernmental Committee on Economic, Trade, and Scientific-Technological Cooperation, thereby creating new momentum for bilateral relations in the years ahead.
On his part, President Putin affirmed that Vietnam remains a trusted and priority partner in Russia's policy toward the Asia-Pacific region.

The Russian President expressed appreciation for General Secretary and State President Lam's invitation and affirmed Russia's support and readiness to closely coordinate with Vietnam to ensure the success of APEC Year 2027.
President Putin also proposed that both sides effectively implement cooperation projects of long-term strategic significance, particularly in the energy sector.
He emphasized Russia's willingness to share experience and technology and to support Vietnam in training human resources in the field of energy.
Regarding economic, trade, and investment cooperation, both sides agreed to promote collaboration in areas where they possess strengths and significant potential.
These include traditional and emerging energy sectors such as nuclear power, wind power, and gas-fired power generation.
The two countries also agreed to improve the efficiency of existing oil and gas joint ventures and expand cooperation in liquefied natural gas (LNG).

In addition, they committed to enhancing cooperation in science and technology, innovation, digital transformation, and the development of a highly skilled workforce to meet each country's development needs.

The two sides also discussed the timely resolution of difficulties and obstacles in order to facilitate stronger business connectivity and expanded cooperation between enterprises from both countries.
The two leaders highly praised the strong progress in tourism, education and training, and people-to-people exchanges between Vietnam and Russia.
General Secretary and President Lam welcomed President Putin's decision to grant visa-free entry to Vietnamese citizens holding ordinary passports.
He noted that this policy would help promote tourism and people-to-people exchanges, strengthen mutual understanding, and deepen ties between the peoples of the two countries.
Exchanging views on regional and international issues, the two leaders emphasized the importance of maintaining peace, security, and stability, while strengthening dialogue and cooperation.
They also underscored the role of multilateralism, the United Nations, and the fundamental principles of international law.
Both sides discussed directions for enhancing cooperation within APEC and ASEAN frameworks, contributing to peace, stability, cooperation, and development in the region and around the world.
